title: Components and signs of the ordinary bounded dual and bidual
statement:
Let $(C,J,R)$ be a small ringed site with commutative coefficient sheaf under [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $E$ be a cochain complex of $R$-module sheaves, with $E^i=0$ for $i<a$ or $b<i$, where $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. Put $O=R[0]$, $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,O)$, and $D'=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(D,O)$ using [def-pur-hom-complex], and write $T^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(T,R)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Projection to the unique possibly nonzero factor gives canonical isomorphisms
$$D^q\cong(E^{-q})^\vee,\qquad (D')^i\cong((E^i)^\vee)^\vee.$$
Under them,
$$d_D^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi d_E^{-q-1},\qquad d_{D'}^i=-(d_E^i)^{\vee\vee},$$
and $D^q=0$ for $q<-b$ or $-a<q$. The homogeneous formula $x\mapsto(\phi\mapsto(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x))$ defines a chain map $\beta:E\to D'$; its degree-$i$ component, under the displayed identification, is $(-1)^i\delta_{E^i}$, where $\delta_T(t)(\phi)=\phi(t)$. These identifications and formulas hold for arbitrary $E$ with the stated bound, with no finite-free retract or exactness assumption on its terms.

proof.text: For each object $U$ and integer $q$, [def-pur-hom-complex] identifies $D^q(U)$ with the families $(f^p)_p$ of maps $E^p|_U\to O^{p+q}|_U$. If $p\ne -q$, the target is zero, so that component has exactly one value, the zero map. Projection to $p=-q$ is therefore inverse to insertion of a map $E^{-q}|_U\to R|_U$ with all other components zero. Both operations are $R(U)$-linear and commute with restriction. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom] these are inverse morphisms of module sheaves $D^q\cong(E^{-q})^\vee$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product and differential formulas; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, second proof paragraph, ordinary dual terms and evaluation up to sign.

proof.text: If $q<-b$, then $-q>b$, and if $-a<q$, then $-q<a$. In either case $E^{-q}=0$ by the assumed bound. There is exactly one module-sheaf map from the zero sheaf to $R$, so [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives $(E^{-q})^\vee=0$. Step 1 gives $D^q=0$. This also covers $a>b$, when every $E^p$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product and differential formulas; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, second proof paragraph, ordinary dual terms and evaluation up to sign.

proof.text: The differential of $O=R[0]$ is zero. In the component $p=-q-1$, the defining differential in [def-pur-hom-complex] consequently reads $(d_D^q f)^{-q-1}=-(-1)^q f^{-q}d_E^{-q-1}$. Under the projection of step 1 this is exactly $d_D^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi d_E^{-q-1}$. All other components have zero target.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product and differential formulas; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, second proof paragraph, ordinary dual terms and evaluation up to sign.

proof.text:
Apply the insertion/projection construction of step 1 with source $D$ and degree $i$: $(D')^i\cong(D^{-i})^\vee\cong((E^i)^\vee)^\vee$. In these identifications a local $\Psi\in(D')^i$ is a map $(E^i)^\vee\to R$. For a local $\chi\in(E^{i+1})^\vee$, the differential formula of [def-pur-hom-complex], followed by step 3 at $q=-i-1$, gives
$$ (d_{D'}^i\Psi)(\chi)=(-1)^{i+1}\Psi(d_D^{-i-1}\chi)=(-1)^{i+1}(-1)^{-i}\Psi(\chi d_E^i)=-\Psi(\chi d_E^i). $$
Here linearity pulls the sign through $\Psi$. The double dual of $d_E^i$ is, by precomposition twice, precisely $\Psi\mapsto(\chi\mapsto\Psi(\chi d_E^i))$, proving the claimed minus sign.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product and differential formulas; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, second proof paragraph, ordinary dual terms and evaluation up to sign.

proof.text: For any module sheaf $T$ and $t\in T(U)$, define $\delta_T(t)$ over the slice at $U$ by sending, for every $V\to U$, a local map $\phi:T|_V\to R|_V$ to $\phi_V(t|_V)$. The rule in [def-pur-sheaf-hom] shows directly that this is a map of sheaves $(T^\vee)|_U\to R|_U$: evaluation commutes with restriction and is linear in $\phi$. It is also linear in $t$ and compatible with varying $U$. Thus $\delta_T:T\to T^{\vee\vee}$ is defined without a reflexivity assumption. If $x$ has degree $i$ and $\phi$ has degree $q$ in $D$, then $\phi(x)$ lies in $O^{i+q}$ and is zero unless $q=-i$. In that unique possibly nonzero degree, $(-1)^{iq}=(-1)^{-i^2}=(-1)^i$, since $i^2-i$ is even. Hence the homogeneous formula in the statement defines degreewise sheaf morphisms $\beta^i=(-1)^i\delta_{E^i}$ under step 4.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product and differential formulas; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, second proof paragraph, ordinary dual terms and evaluation up to sign.

proof.text:
It remains to check the chain-map equation. For $x\in E^i(U)$ and every $\chi\in(E^{i+1})^\vee(V)$ on every $V\to U$, steps 4 and 5 give
$$ (d_{D'}^i\beta^i(x))_V(\chi)=-(-1)^i\chi_V(d_E^i(x)|_V)=(-1)^{i+1}\chi_V(d_E^i(x)|_V)=(\beta^{i+1}(d_E^i x))_V(\chi). $$
These equalities for all $V$ and $\chi$ are equality of the sheaf maps of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]; thus $d_{D'}^i\beta^i=\beta^{i+1}d_E^i$ in every degree. This is the definition of a chain map in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Every calculation used only the Hom definitions and the stated bound, so no exactness or finite-free retract hypothesis has entered.
